entities.summary: Yoaz Hendel is an Israeli politician and public figure who served as Minister of Communications and as a member of the Knesset. He is also an author, publicist, public activist, businessman, and a battalion commander in the reserves. Additionally, he is the founder and chairman of the Miluimnikim ("Reservists") Movement. Hendel holds a doctorate in history and previously served as a lecturer in the Department of Political Science at Bar-Ilan University. Before entering politics, he worked in the defense establishment, was a journalist and columnist, hosted radio and television programs, and served as head of the Institute for Zionist Strategies.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a battalion commander in the reserves and founder of the Miluimnikim ('Reservists') Movement, Hendel has played a significant role in shaping Israel's defense policies and public discourse on reserve service. His efforts have had a notable impact on Israel's military and social landscape.
